title: Tensorization of a two-function inequality
statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets, with probability laws $
u_A,
u_B$ and couplings $ho_A,ho_B$ on $A\times A$ and $B\times B$, respectively. Let $p,q>0$, and suppose that for each of the two spaces the coupling expectation of $u(x)v(y)$ is at most the product of the $p$-norm of $u$ and the $q$-norm of $v$, for every pair of real-valued functions. Then the product coupling on $(A\times B)\times(A\times B)$ satisfies the same inequality for every pair of real-valued functions on $A\times B$, with norms taken under the product law $\nu_A\times\nu_B$.
hypotheses_covered: $\nu_A$ and $\nu_B$ are probability laws on $A$ and $B$
$\rho_A$ and $\rho_B$ are probability laws on $A\times A$ and $B\times B$
The two-function inequality holds for all real-valued functions on $A$ under $\nu_A,\rho_A$
The two-function inequality holds for all real-valued functions on $B$ under $\nu_B,\rho_B$
$f,g$ are arbitrary real-valued functions on $A\times B$
